speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with sudden-onset vertigo. To determine the cause, have you experienced any hearing loss, tinnitus, or dizziness triggered by changes in head position?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).

Based on your history of sudden-onset spinning sensation lasting only 3 minutes while lying down, with no hearing loss or neurological deficits, the clinical presentation is classic for BPPV. This condition is caused by calcium crystals in the inner ear becoming dislodged.
